title: Deterministic Envelope & Retry Semantics for Tool-Enabled Streamed Responses
creator: Ava Chen
description: Short PRD: Define a deterministic envelope format, explicit retry and idempotency semantics, and graceful degradation modes for streamed responses that include tool/function invocations. Goal is to make behavior testable and resilient across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments while enabling SDKs and SDK clients to implement reliable parsing and retry logic.
background: Current issues observed in field and tests: 1) partial streamed JSON fragments that reference tool calls can be ambiguous for downstream parsers; 2) retries during streaming sometimes cause duplicate tool invocations or conflicting state; 3) fallbacks to non-streamed responses are ad hoc across SDKs. This ticket consolidates acceptance criteria and scoped requirements to make behavior deterministic and measurable.
user_stories: As an SDK engineer, I need a stable envelope and event markers so the client can resume/parsing without risking double tool execution.
As a platform user, I want retries to be safe (idempotent) when network flaps occur during streamed tool handoffs.
As an SRE, I need clear telemetry points to diagnose partial emissions, retry triggers, and tool gateway failures.
requirements: Define a top-level 'envelope' structure for streamed responses that delineates event types: token, partial_object, tool_call_start, tool_call_event, tool_call_end, error, end_of_stream.

Mandate canonical event fields: event_id (UUID), stream_pos (monotonic integer), timestamp (RFC3339), type (one of the event types), payload (stringified or encoded blob), and checksum (optional) — all fields must be present as strings.
Tool invocation handshake: tool_call_start must include tool_id, call_id (UUID), expected_schema, and idempotency_key. Subsequent tool_call_event messages must reference call_id.

Retry semantics: if client reconnects and provides last_ack_stream_pos, server must resume from next event; server must not re-emit tool_call_start for a call_id already acknowledged unless idempotency_key indicates safe replay.

Fallback mode: if streaming cannot be sustained within a configurable timebox (default 3s), server should emit a terminal 'fallback' event with a coherent non-streamed result that conforms to the same output schema.
Error classification: classify errors into transient, permanent, and tool-gateway. Each error event must include a standardized error_code and human_readable_hint.
Client-side parse requirements: SDKs must be able to reconstruct partial objects and verify call boundaries using event_id, stream_pos, and call_id without requiring full-stream buffering.
Backpressure and pacing: server must expose pacing_hint events when queueing/backpressure occurs; SDKs may surface UX indicators but must continue to honor resume semantics.
Metrics hooks: emit structured logs/events for tool_call_start, tool_call_end, tool_retry, fallback_emitted, stream_resume, and stream_abort with call_id and session_id tags.
Security considerations: tool payloads may contain sensitive data; tool_call_event payloads must support optional encryption metadata and KMS reference IDs in production/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Envelope contract conformance: unit tests validate serialization and parsing of every event type; fuzz tests confirm parsers tolerate out-of-order arrival but enforce monotonic stream_pos during normal operation.

Resume and retry tests: integration test that simulates mid-stream disconnect verifies that client reconnect with last_ack_stream_pos resumes without re-triggering side-effecting tool executions when idempotency_key is unchanged.

Tool idempotency verification: system tests for tool gateways confirm that repeated tool_call_start with same idempotency_key does not create duplicate side effects and returns the original tool result with a deterministic status (cached or deduped).

Fallback behavior: e2e test demonstrating streaming degrades to a single non-stream JSON payload within the configured timebox, and that payload validates against the same output schema as streamed final state.
Error classification and SDK surface: SDK integration tests ensure clients receive standardized error_code and human_readable_hint and map them to retry/no-retry decisions per the spec.

Observability: dashboards show counts and latency distributions for stream_resume, stream_abort, tool_retry, and fallback_emitted; alert fires when tool_retry rate increases by >5x baseline in 5m window.
Performance: additional end-to-end latency overhead introduced by envelope metadata must be <2% at p50 and <5% at p95 for the target workload used in runtime benchmark suite.

Compatibility: hosted and dedicated runtimes must emit identical envelope events for the same model + request parameters; differences for private deployments must be documented and gated behind configuration flags.
monitoring_and_metrics: Metric: stream_resume_count tagged by model, region, tenant
Metric: tool_retry_count tagged by tool_id and idempotency_key_result (hit/miss)
Log event: fallback_emitted with session_id, cause_reason, time_to_fallback_ms
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) API contract and unit tests merged; 2) SDK updates in canary (Node, Python); 3) Enable envelope on 10% of traffic for non-critical models (runtime flag); 4) Monitor metrics and increase to 100% after 72h with no regression; 5) Document behavior for Dedicated/Private and add configuration options for enterprise customers.
open_questions: Should checksum field be required or optional (storage/CPU tradeoff)?
How should the platform indicate that a tool result was served from a cache vs recomputed? (explicit field or status code)
Do we allow client-side dark launches that ignore envelope fields for backwards compatibility, and if so what's the deprecation timeline?
